story: Gary and Donna are out on the reserved pickleball court at the Rec Center, where Donna is coaching him to soft-dink from the kitchen line while an afternoon shower drifts over Sumter Oaks. Hal is strolling down Magnolia Loop toward the Rec Center with the dutiful air of a man who has been asked to deliver something important. Back at her house, Rosa is sitting at her kitchen table drafting the Saturday menu and writing out her grocery and borrow list, determined to have everything in order before the weekend.
events: Gary (pickleball court 1): Practice dinks with Donna on the reserved court
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Draft the Saturday menu and write out a grocery and borrow list

gary.thought_process: Donna reserved the court for two hours and told me to grab a paddle and work on my dink shot. I already apologized and told her about the form, so no need to repeat any of that. Last tick I stepped onto court 1 to warm up, so the natural next move is to actually play. Dinner at Rosa's is coming up and I promised to be on time, so I'll keep an eye on the clock. Pickleball keeps me connected to Donna and Hal, which matters more to me than I let on. The cart wiring can wait for Architectural Review.

parameters.content: Practice dinks with Donna on the reserved court

donna.thought_process: Gary just stepped onto court 1 to warm up, and I already reserved our two-hour slot and told him to grab a paddle and work on his dink shot. No need to ask or invite again. The best move is to actually get him playing: give him one concrete pointer on the dink and get a rally going. Dinner with Rosa is at six, so we have limited time and should make it count.

parameters.content: Perfect, you're loose. Stay at the kitchen line and just pop it soft over the net, no swinging. Think of it like tucking in a baby, and we'll rally till the shower picks up.

hal.thought_process: Donna trimmed her flamingos to three, so that complaint is basically dead. I've already checked the bulletin board and the mailbox with no reply from Architectural Review, and nobody's around to talk to. Gary's cart still needs a ruling, and Gary and Donna both headed to the Rec Center. Rosa's dinner is Saturday at six. Best use of this hour is to walk over to the Rec Center and see whether Gary's cart is parked there, or catch him in person, since that's where my enforcement goal and the neighborly stuff both lead.

parameters.content: Heading to the Rec Center to find Gary and check on his cart, and see whether the committee has posted anything there.

rosa.thought_process: It's 5:17 PM Tuesday and I'm alone at home. The last few ticks I've been prepping: place settings counted, tablecloth and platters out, chair count confirmed for four guests plus me. Shift schedule already checked. Gary still hasn't given me a firm yes or a dish, and the dinner is Saturday at six. The kitchen is the one place I haven't wrapped up, so I'll finish what's left there instead of repeating table tasks. Nobody's around to talk to, and moving out in the afternoon shower wouldn't help.

parameters.content: Draft the Saturday menu and write out a grocery and borrow list

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
